questions.question: When should you give up your right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at controlled intersections.
Whenever it helps prevent a crash.
Never. It confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it helps prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Give up your right-of-way whenever it helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To see around the sides of the vehicle.
Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before passing them.
Because following too closely will catch you in the vehicle's slipstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicle drivers may not see you if you drive directly behind them. Increase your following distance behind trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles towing trailers. This gives you a better view around the sides so you can see the road ahead.

questions.question: What is the most important thing to remember about slowing down for curves?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle's inertia may make it hard to turn. To stay in control, you must slow down before entering the curve.

questions.question: What do broken yellow lines mean on streets and highways?

options.text: No passing zone.
Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken line means passing is allowed when it is safe.

questions.question: If your car skids, which direction should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: Keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go. Once the vehicle straightens out, turn the steering wheel back the other way.

questions.question: Is it legal to drive faster than the speed limit when passing another vehicle?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You must never exceed the posted speed limit, even when passing another vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reduce your speed when the pavement is wet.
The road ahead has a series of turns or curves.
Traffic increases ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that the road will be slippery when wet. Reduce your speed when you see this sign.

questions.question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes to the left, you should look:

options.text: Over your right shoulder.
At your side mirror.
Over your left shoulder.
At your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you should turn into:

options.text: Any lane.
The first lane.
The second lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The first lane.
questions.explanation: When making any turn, turn from the lane closest to your direction into the first available legal lane. When turning from a two-way street to a one-way street, turn into the first lane.

questions.question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Overcorrect.
Turn your steering wheel into traffic.
Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
Release the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle begins to skid, stay calm. Steer in the direction of the skid.

questions.question: When a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what should you do?

options.text: You can still turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
You can no longer turn and must go straight.
You still have the right to turn.
You do not have to turn in the direction the arrow pointed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can still turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you can still turn in the direction the arrow pointed. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When can you legally turn left at a red light after stopping?

options.text: When you are on a two-way street turning onto a two-way street.
When you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street.
When you yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After a complete stop, you can turn left at a red light only if you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street. Make sure no signs forbid this turn.

questions.question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and you can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction and you can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and you cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Continue on the freeway and find another route.
Go to the next exit, leave the freeway, and come back to the correct exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Do not back up in the travel lane or on the shoulder. Keep driving to the next exit or crossroad instead. Other drivers do not expect a vehicle backing up and this can cause a crash.

questions.question: When must you pull over for an emergency vehicle?

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: You must pull to the right edge of the road and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights, whether it is coming from behind or from the opposite direction.

questions.question: What are signs called that require drivers to obey their instructions?

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs require drivers to obey their instructions. Breaking this rule can result in a penalty.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Stop ahead.
Construction or roadwork is happening.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction or roadwork is happening.
questions.explanation: Orange diamond-shaped signs warn of construction, maintenance, and utility work areas. These signs help keep drivers and pedestrians safe. Traffic fines can be doubled in these areas.

questions.question: If another car is passing you in a no passing zone, what should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Keep your speed and position the same.
Slow down to let them safely return to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to let them safely return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Slow down to help the other vehicle return to the lane easily. This helps everyone avoid hazards ahead.

questions.question: You see a steady yellow light ahead and have not entered the intersection yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get through before it turns red.
Slow down and carefully go through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a steady yellow light and have not entered the intersection, stop safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through at a safe speed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead curves only to the right.
The road ahead turns sharply to the right.
The road curves right and then left.
The road curves left and then right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right and then left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns that the road curves to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: When are streets and highways most slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just after it starts to rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery when rain first starts. Water mixes with oil and dirt on the road that has not washed away yet. Drive slowly and carefully during the first 30 minutes of rain.

questions.question: As you approach the top of a hill, you should:

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Prepare to stop, if needed.
Maintain a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop, if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill. A vehicle might be stopped just out of sight. Slow down so you can stop if necessary.

questions.question: If heavy smoke covers the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers and continue.
Reduce your speed, move as far to the right as possible, and stop off the roadway.
Turn on your high beam headlights and continue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed, move as far to the right as possible, and stop off the roadway.
questions.explanation: Slow down right away. Move to the right and stop off the road. Check if it is safe to continue before driving again. Heavy smoke can hurt your eyes and lungs.

questions.question: If another car is following you too closely on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to drive around you.
Speed up to increase the distance between you and the other car.
Apply your brakes to slow down, then resume your original speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to drive around you.
questions.explanation: If safe, change lanes. If you cannot change lanes, slowly reduce your speed. This will encourage the other driver to pass you.

questions.question: When driving past a vehicle that just parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Assume that the driver will open the car door as you approach.
Speed up.
Slam on your brakes.
Assume that the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume that the driver will open the car door as you approach.
questions.explanation: Expect the driver to open the door as you pass. Be extra careful when driving near parked cars.

questions.question: You reach a four-way stop at the same time as a driver on your left. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left has the right-of-way.
You have the right-of-way.
Whoever is signaling to make a turn has the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: Oncoming cars are to your left and parked cars are to your right. Where should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: Steer down the middle between the oncoming cars and parked cars.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) does NOT depend on:

options.text: Your body weight.
How much you drink.
How much time passes between drinks.
How physically fit you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Physical fitness does not affect BAC.

questions.question: If the rear of your vehicle skids to the left, you should:

options.text: Not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.
Turn your steering wheel to the right to correct the skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.
questions.explanation: If you skid, take your foot off the gas and do not use the brakes. Turn the wheel in the direction the rear is sliding. If you have anti-lock brakes, press firmly on the brakes and steer straight.

questions.question: What does a speed limit sign mean?

options.text: Only a recommended driving speed.
The exact speed at which you must travel to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.
The maximum safe driving speed under all road conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the highest legal speed for that road when conditions are good. You may need to drive slower when weather or road conditions are poor.
